descriptionChirho: To obey or observe laws, commandments, or precepts faithfully; to comply with established rules or divine instructions. The object is typically an abstract norm: commandments, the law, or apostolic decrees. Arabic حَفِظ (to keep/preserve in the sense of obey), Hebrew שָׁמַר/שׁוֹמֵר (keep/observe -- the classic OT covenant verb), Hindi पालन–करना/मानना (to follow/obey), Korean 지키다 (keep/observe), Spanish guardar (keep/guard). Found in the rich young ruler's claim to have kept the commandments (Matt 19:20, Mark 10:20, Luke 18:21), Jesus' pronouncement about those who keep the word (Luke 11:28, John 12:47), Stephen's accusation about failing to keep the law (Acts 7:53), the apostolic decree's instructions (Acts 16:4), Paul on circumcision and law-keeping (Rom 2:26, Gal 6:13), and Timothy's charge (1 Tim 5:21).

To keep watch over a person, place, or thing as a sentinel or custodian; to serve as a physical guard or sentry. The focus is on vigilant surveillance and physical custody rather than moral obedience. Arabic يَحْرُس/حَافِظ (to guard/be a guardian), Hebrew שׁוֹמֵר/לְהִשָּׁמֵר (watchman/be guarded), Hindi रखवाली–करना/पहरा–देना (to keep watch/stand guard), Korean 지키다 (guard -- same verb but in custodial context), Spanish custodiar/guardar (to guard/watch). Found of shepherds keeping watch over flocks (Luke 2:8), the demoniac being kept under guard (Luke 8:29), the strong man guarding his house (Luke 11:21), soldiers guarding Peter in prison (Acts 12:4), Paul under guard at Caesarea (Acts 23:35, 28:16), and Stephen's garments being guarded by Saul (Acts 22:20).

To keep safe from danger, destruction, or spiritual loss; to preserve or protect something or someone entrusted to one's care. The emphasis is on safeguarding rather than either obedience (sense 1) or physical surveillance (sense 2). Arabic احْفَظ/حَفِظ (preserve/guard), Hebrew שָׁמַר/שְׁמֹר (guard/preserve), Hindi बचाना/रक्षित–करना/सुरक्षित–रखना (to save/protect/keep safe), Korean 보호하다/보존하다/지키다 (protect/preserve/guard), Spanish proteger/guardar (protect/guard). Found of Jesus protecting his own (John 12:25 -- guarding one's life; John 17:12 -- 'I guarded them'), God's faithfulness in guarding believers (2 Thess 3:3), Paul's charge to guard the deposit (1 Tim 6:20, 2 Tim 1:12, 1:14), God's preservation of Noah (2 Pet 2:5), John's call to guard from idols (1 John 5:21), and Jude's doxology about the one who is able to keep them from stumbling (Jude 1:24).

Middle voice usage: to be on one's guard against something harmful, to take precautions, to beware. The reflexive middle voice (φυλάσσεσθε, φυλάσσου) shifts the meaning from 'guard an object' to 'guard oneself from a danger.' Arabic احْتَرِسُوا/احْذَر (be cautious/beware), Hebrew הִשָּׁמְרוּ/הִשָּׁמֵר (be on guard/beware -- Niphal reflexive of שׁמר), Hindi बचो/सावधान–रहो (escape/be cautious), Korean 조심하라 (be careful), Spanish guardaos/guárdate (guard yourselves). Found in Jesus' warning to beware of covetousness (Luke 12:15), the apostolic decree's instruction to keep from certain practices (Acts 21:25), Paul's warning to Timothy against Alexander (2 Tim 4:15), and Peter's admonition to guard against being carried away by error (2 Pet 3:17).
